<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-fresh-herbs" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-fresh-herbs-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of fresh herbs, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>183</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Angelon-Gaetz et al. 2018</td><td>2</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Winiarska-Mieczan et al. 2023</td><td>1</td><td>33%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for fresh herbs, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>3 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li><li><a href="../sources/angelon-gaetz2018-lead-spices-north-carolina" class="internal" data-slug="sources/angelon-gaetz2018-lead-spices-north-carolina" data-no-cite-meta>Angelon-Gaetz et al. 2018</a></li><li><a href="../sources/winiarska-mieczan2023-cd-pb-polish-herbs-spices" class="internal" data-slug="sources/winiarska-mieczan2023-cd-pb-polish-herbs-spices" data-no-cite-meta>Winiarska-Mieczan et al. 2023</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach fresh Herbs

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>

<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach fresh Herbs comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Fresh Herbs, as sold from leaf, western Anatolia had Zn higher at 83,700 µg/kg, against 11,200 µg/kg for leaf, western Anatolia in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/divrikli2006-spices-herbal-plants-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Divrikli U, Horzum N, Soylak M, Elci L · 2006</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/divrikli2006-spices-herbal-plants-metals">Trace heavy metal contents of some spices and herbal plants from western Anatolia, Turkey</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/divrikli2006-spices-herbal-plants-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/divrikli2006-spices-herbal-plants-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Divrikli U, Horzum N, Soylak M, Elci L · 2006</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/divrikli2006-spices-herbal-plants-metals">Trace heavy metal contents of some spices and herbal plants from western Anatolia, Turkey</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/divrikli2006-spices-herbal-plants-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.



<a id="sampling-and-testing"></a>
## Testing fresh Herbs for metals

<a id="hmi-ing-025"></a>
<a id="what-sampling-design-is-appropriate-for-the-ingredient-heterogeneity-lot-and-decision"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-026"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-027"></a>
<a id="what-can-a-certificate-of-analysis-or-non-detect-establish-and-what-remains-untested"></a>

Results depend on the method and its reporting limit. Reporting limits for lead ranged from 0.83 µg/kg (Altıkulaç et al. 2025) to 10,000 µg/kg (Sultana et al. 2022), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup No source in the library converted fresh Herbs concentrations into a verified estimate of intake for a defined population. Concentrations describe the food, not individual risk.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.


<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Fresh Herbs FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-fresh-herbs" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-fresh-herbs" data-question="What heavy metals are found in fresh Herbs?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in fresh Herbs?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, total mercury, methylmercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, As, Ba, Hg, Sr and Ti in fresh Herbs, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/abdolahpour2023-heavy-metals-babol-vegetables|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Abdolahpour Alamdari H, Sleman Ali H, Sadighara P, Jahed Khaniki G, Shahsavanpoor Landeh K, Dehghani MH · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/abdolahpour2023-heavy-metals-babol-vegetables">The health risk assessment of heavy metals in vegetables grown in Babol city, Iran</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Archives of Health Sciences</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/abdolahpour2023-heavy-metals-babol-vegetables">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/angelon-gaetz2018-lead-spices-north-carolina|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Angelon-Gaetz KA, Klaus C, Chaudhry EA, Bean DK · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/angelon-gaetz2018-lead-spices-north-carolina">Lead in Spices, Herbal Remedies, and Ceremonial Powders Sampled from Home Investigations for Children with Elevated Blood Lead Levels — North Carolina, 2011–2018</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/angelon-gaetz2018-lead-spices-north-carolina">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bora FD, Bunea A, Pop SR, Banita SI, Dusa DS, Chira A, Bunea CI · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing">Quantification and Reduction in Heavy results in 5 reporting regions, with subgroup medians from 2.6 to 1,300 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-fresh-herbs" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-fresh-herbs" data-question="How do heavy metals get into fresh Herbs?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into fresh Herbs?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, fresh Herbs from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than fresh Herbs from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/divrikli2006-spices-herbal-plants-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Divrikli U, Horzum N, Soylak M, Elci L · 2006</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/divrikli2006-spices-herbal-plants-metals">Trace heavy metal contents of some spices and herbal plants from western Anatolia, Turkey</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/divrikli2006-spices-herbal-plants-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Fresh Herbs, as sold from leaf, western Anatolia had cadmium higher at 1,700 µg/kg, against 500 µg/kg for leaf, western Anatolia in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/divrikli2006-spices-herbal-plants-metals|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Divrikli U, Horzum N, Soylak M, Elci L · 2006</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/divrikli2006-spices-herbal-plants-metals">Trace heavy metal contents of some spices and herbal plants from western Anatolia, Turkey</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/divrikli2006-spices-herbal-plants-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-fresh-herbs" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-fresh-herbs" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in fresh Herbs?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in fresh Herbs?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, fresh Herbs, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (2.6 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (1,300 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in EURO (12.5 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (138 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-fresh-herbs-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-fresh-herbs-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in fresh Herbs is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in fresh Herbs is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 8 results from 1 source, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported inorganic arsenic in fresh Herbs, as sold from 54 results in 2 reporting regions, with subgroup medians from 39.5 to 200 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
